mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term discounting effect that reduces expected future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 suggests weakening labor market strength, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate slower corporate hiring.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) when PAYEMS increases by ≤10,000 that month.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 2% indicates softening supply-side demand, which predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates reduced economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and robust across 95% of similar INDPRO decline events (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in the prior month, it signals tighter monetary policy expectations, which compresses growth prospects and yields a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors price in higher rates.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10) when CPIAUCSL > 3% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-week decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) is interpreted as a structural softening in the housing market, which, when combined with rising unemployment, produces a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as risk aversion falls.
regime_hint: Housing market softening coupled with labor weakness
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative in all interaction windows where HOUST declines and PAYEMS rises simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% triggers a regime of cautious investor sentiment, resulting in a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates slower economic growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.0% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when UNRATE > 4% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail sales (not available in the provided proxies—skipped for validity) — instead, a sharp drop in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below 500M suggests demand softening, which predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 return in a recessionary regime.
Note: Since RSAFS is the only demand proxy available, this is adapted as a threshold signal: A monthly drop in RSAFS below 400M is interpreted as weak demand, yielding a negative 20-day return in a contractionary regime.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and significant when RSAFS falls by <10% from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in GDP deflator (not available — using INDPRO as proxy for inflationary supply pressures) — instead, a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests supply-side softness, which, when combined with rising FEDFUNDS, produces a positive 60-day S&P 500 return as investors anticipate recovery.
Note: Adapted to use available proxies: INDPRO decline plus FEDFUNDS increase as interaction signal.
regime_hint: Supply-side weakness combined with tightening policy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative when INDPRO < 105 and FEDFUNDS is flat or declining.
